title: json-boolean/v1 model
description: Authoring aid for models with profile json-boolean/v1. Go validation in jsonvalidator is authoritative. This schema cannot express: unique property names within one object; duplicate JSON keys; trailing data; the 1 MiB size limit; JSON nesting depth 64; schema depth 32; and the 512 schema node limit. It also cannot express: plain unsigned integer source spelling for length bounds (JSON.parse erases decimal and exponent spelling, and numeric -0 passes the nonnegative bound); minLength not above maxLength; the 256-byte limit on const and enum strings (a pattern cannot count bytes); and the refusal of control characters and U+FFFD in those strings in every spelling. It does check the exact members of each node shape, which string members may be combined, unique enum values and enum size 1 to 32, parsed length bounds as integer values 0 to 65535, property name syntax, at most 128 properties per object and that additionalProperties is a boolean.

node.description: One shape of the predicate. Object nodes say whether extra input properties are allowed with additionalProperties true or false.

oneOf.description: A JSON string, with no further rule.
A JSON string equal to one value, compared exactly.
A JSON string equal to one of 1 to 32 unique values, compared exactly.

A JSON string whose length in code points is within the bounds. At least one bound is present. Go checks minLength not above maxLength and requires plain unsigned integer source spelling; the schema sees only parsed numeric values.
A JSON boolean, optionally fixed to one value.
An array whose every element satisfies items.
An object with at most 128 named properties. Names must be unique (Go checks).
